desc: Build exact brute-force/reverse-BFS solver and reduction verifier harness for small alphabets/lengths.
Establish reduction ans = min_B [runs(B) + inv(A,B)] (proven analytically: swap-to-B upper bound; batch-order/inversion lower bound).
Establish that only cost-1 jumps (length-1 run crossing a length-1 run) can strictly help: cost≥2 merges are net≥0, consume all length-1 runs locally, and never enable future profit.

Establish disjointness: an element that was crossed can never later jump profitably, crossed-twice is impossible, jumpers become immobile — so an optimal B is A with disjoint adjacent pairs swapped, and ans = min over such swap sets of [#swaps + runs(result)].
Design O(N) DP: states (d_{i-2}, d_{i-1}) ∈ {(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}; reconstruct position values from swap bits; accumulate swap cost + run count incrementally.
Implement the final O(N) DP solution per the I/O format (T test cases, sum N ≤ 2e5, one answer per line) — code complete, uses fast buffered input, O(1) extra space per case.

Verify correctness analytically: independent hand-trace of the DP on sample 1 (1 1 2 1 2 → 3, recovering the swap-pair-(2,3) path), sample 2 (all distinct → 4), sample 3 (alternating length 11 → 8 via 3 disjoint swaps + 5 runs), plus edge cases (all equal → 1, all distinct → N, N=2, boundary swaps at i=0 and i=N-1 correctly forced/handled via the `last` flag and first-run initialization). Full proof write-up (reduction theorem + cost-1 sufficiency + disjointness/zipper lemma + DP state correctness) is recorded in the notes.
